Marathon Petroleum has fallen 18.5% over two weeks, with today's decline part of a sharp slide that accelerated after the midterm elections. The primary driver is political risk to the refining industry: a Democratic sweep in Congress signals stronger push for renewable energy and likely tougher environmental regulation, which threatens long-term demand for petroleum products and refinery profitability. Oil prices themselves remain relatively stable—US crude around $100 per barrel and refinery utilization at 94.5%—so the damage isn't coming from weak energy fundamentals, but from investor concerns about the sector's political headwinds.

The timing of the selloff—steepest from November 4th onward, right after election results—confirms this is about policy outlook rather than immediate market conditions. Refinery operators typically benefit from energy scarcity and policy uncertainty, but Democratic control of Congress cuts against both those tailwinds going forward.
